reaction.episode: CORRECTION through Friday Nov 6: SPX 7,376.86, -5.96% from its 120-day high, -3.94% below its 50-day but +0.71% above its 200-day; SMH -30.94% and BELOW Zone 2 ($470-505); NVDA $186.64 BETWEEN_ZONES; VIX 25.64 rolling over from a 28.18 five-day high; HY OAS 3.48 with credit calm; mechanical tally 3 of 4, zone occupancy the missing leg. Data is fresh, not stale.
reaction.invalidation: A daily SPX close above the 7,750-7,820 failure zone with SMH reclaiming $580 and VIX below 20 would void the Watch stance (correction over, not a trap); conversely a sustained HY OAS above 4% voids the ladder's re-entry rungs and turns the episode into a credit event.

ladder.response: Hold cash, no probe. Re-map zones lower and wait for a second-low structure; do not buy the first print below the line.
ladder.trigger: SMH closes below $450 or SPX closes below 7,300 (its 200-day at 7,325.05)

ladder.response: Sell into strength / no chase. Treat the zone as the pivot-and-fail test; require a hold above the zone before any add.
ladder.trigger: Bounce into the failure zone: SPX 7,750-7,820 or SMH 580-600

ladder.response: Full stand-down. Cancel any probe plans and reassess credit before re-arming anything.
ladder.trigger: VIX closes above its 5-day high of 28.18, or HY OAS above 4%

ladder.response: Tranche A re-arms: 25% starter per the deployment ladder, sized off the $2,163.99 cash base.
ladder.trigger: SMH closes inside Zone 2 ($470-505) with VIX below 25 and tally at least 3 of 4

reaction.trapRisk: Friday's bounce (SPX +0.31%, SMH +3.62%) came off Thursday's washout with VIX still at 25.64 — a first bounce, not a confirmation. The pivot-and-fail pattern means entries must not chase it: no probe until the second low near 7,300 holds or a Zone 2 print confirms, and any rally toward 7,750-7,820 is a sell zone, not a buy signal.

strategyPosture: Watch. The correction is real but unconfirmed as a bottom: SMH is below Zone 2, NVDA is between zones, the mechanical tally is 3 of 4 with zone occupancy the missing leg, and VIX at 25.64 is still above the 25 stand-down line — cash stays king until a Zone 2 print and a VIX close under 25 re-arm Tranche A.

themes.counterRead: Cheap on the fundamentals is not the same as buyable now: SMH sits BELOW Zone 2 ($470-505) and NVDA is BETWEEN_ZONES ($175-185 below, $200-210 above), so the mechanical ladder has no Zone 2 print to arm on. The opportunity is real but the entry trigger has not fired — the tape has to print the zone first, not the thesis.
themes.dataAnchor: The drawdown is multiple compression, not a demand collapse. NVDA is -23.3% from its 52-week high at $186.64 while revenue grows 61.4% YoY; AVGO is -40.7% from its high at $293.69 with revenue +55% YoY and a 67.8% gross margin; DDOG is -40.5% with revenue +27.7% YoY; LRCX is -54.3% with revenue +131.3% YoY. 35 dislocations are flagged, nearly all sentiment-driven, with RSI (14-day) of 27-37 across the complex — deeply oversold. SMH is -30.94% from its 120-day high at $463.96.
themes.label: AI complex washout: price far below the fundamentals
themes.narrative: The market is pricing the AI trade as a financing bust: semis and AI infrastructure names are down 20-55% from their highs in a month, with headlines warning the AI cycle itself is the problem.
themes.watchFor: SMH daily close back inside Zone 2 ($470-505) or NVDA close inside $175-185.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and worth tracking, not dismissing: GOOGL is the weakest Mag 7 name at -30.3% from its high while AAPL is the strongest at -3.7%, so the weakness is concentrated, not uniform. If lending standards flip from loose to tight, rotation becomes rollover — the read holds only while credit stays calm.
themes.dataAnchor: The Mag 7 average sits -17.44% from 52-week highs against SPY at only -5.9% — an 11.54-point divergence gap — while bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold). SPY closed Friday at $736.53, +0.48% on the day and -4.83% over one month, and IWM is only -1.38% over one month. Leaders over one month include NXT (+19.14%) and MA (+13.33%). Credit is calm: HY OAS 3.48.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover: Mag 7 lags while the index holds
themes.narrative: Headlines read the tape as a broad market rollover, with the biggest names leading the fall.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS above 4% or SLOOS moving toward the stress zone; Mag 7 gap widening past 15 points.

themes.counterRead: A +15-23% day after a -31% month is bounce mechanics, not confirmed demand — the sector's narrative is running ahead of everything except VST's print. VST itself is only at step one of its entry conditions: a close holding inside $106-130, still needing a $132.66 reclaim and then the 50-day at $145.08. Chasing the sector's Friday spike is buying the bounce, not the print.
themes.dataAnchor: The one-day moves are extreme: OKLO +23.18% and SMR +15.56% on Friday, CCJ +5.05%, URA +4.20% — but all of them come off brutal one-month drawdowns (OKLO -31.59%, SMR -31.01%, CCJ -17.61%). The one anchored leg is VST: +10.42% Friday to $124.80 after its Q3 print (reported Nov 6), still -36.6% from its high, with insiders having bought $1.17M at the trough and a top-conviction score of 80 on revenue +19.1% YoY.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power: a violent oversold bounce on one real print
themes.narrative: Nuclear power is being repriced as the AI trade's next leg, with Friday's tape showing the sector ripping higher.
themes.watchFor: VST daily close holding inside $106-130, then a $132.66 reclaim; OKLO/SMR giving back Friday's spike on no news.

themes.counterRead: Calm credit and a steepening curve agree with the rotation read, but the data week decides whether that holds: CPI Oct lands Tuesday Nov 10 (HIGH signal strength), FOMC minutes Nov 18, and the December FOMC decision Dec 8-9. A hot CPI print reprices the December path and can flip credit from calm to cracking fast — the calm is conditional on the prints.
themes.dataAnchor: The rates picture is orderly, not stressed: 10-year 4.84%, 2-year 4.46%, 30-year 5.25%, with the 2s10s curve at +0.38 (steepening, not inverting), real 10-year 2.61%, DFF 3.88%, and HY OAS 3.48 with credit calm. VIX closed 25.64, down 9.01% on the day and rolling over from its 5-day high of 28.18.
themes.label: Rates and credit: calm tape into a heavy data week
themes.narrative: Rate-hike fears dominate the macro tape, with December policy the open question and the curve the battleground.
themes.watchFor: CPI Oct Tue Nov 10 8:30am; HY OAS above 4%; VIX closing back above its 5-day high of 28.18.

whereWaveBuilds: The next move materializes at the second-low test near SPX 7,300: SPX closed Friday at 7,376.86, only +0.71% above its 200-day (7,325.05) and -3.94% below its 50-day. A hold there with volume plus a Zone 2 print is the buyable setup; a close below 7,300 opens the 7,020-7,200 band.
